Seminar Title:

Design of Adaptive Energy-Harvesting and Attack-Resilient Cognitive Radio Networks: From Terrestrial Sensing to UAV-assisted Access

Abstract:

With the rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT)-based applications and the deployment of dense
5G networks, spectrum scarcity has become a critical challenge. In this context, cognitive radio networks
(CRNs) have emerged as an intelligent wireless paradigm to solve spectrum scarcity by enabling dynamic
spectrum access (DSA) for secondary users (SUs), allowing them to opportunistically use underutilized bands
of primary users (PUs). Integrating UAVs into CRNs further enhances received signal strength, coverage,
spectrum utilization efficiency (SUE), and network throughput due to their flexible and dynamic deployment
capabilities, making UAV-CRNs particularly relevant for 5G and future 6G applications. Consequently,
achieving high sensing performance, improved SUE, energy efficiency (EE), and robust security has become
a central research priority. This dissertation addresses these challenges through four core contributions. In
the first contribution, a collaborative decision-based spectrum sensing (CDSS) approach with an adaptive
decision threshold mechanism is proposed to ensure robust sensing performance by effectively balancing PU
protection and dynamic spectrum access, thereby reducing the decision error probability under low-SNR
conditions. In the second contribution, a PU state transition model with possible SU transmission cases
is analyzed under both perfect and imperfect sensing scenarios to achieve effective spectrum utilization,
while a joint optimization of the decision threshold and sensing duration is further proposed to maximize
spectrum utilization efficiency (SUE). In the third contribution, an efficient dynamic resource allocation
technique is proposed for an energy-harvesting-enabled UAV-CRN framework, in which the UAV performs
sensing and communication tasks by harvesting ambient RF energy, thereby improving energy efficiency
(EE). Finally, in the fourth contribution, an intelligent, secure spectrum sensing technique is proposed to
address the security vulnerabilities in UAV-CRNs. These contributions collectively offer robust and practical
solutions that facilitate the evolution of next-generation 5G/6G CRNs, ensuring improved SUE, EE, secure
communication, and reliable performance.
